newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rock star Danko denies drug smuggling in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Rock star Danko denies drug smuggling in Japan.

text.p: Canadian rock star Rick Danko has denied charges of colluding with his wife to smuggle heroin into Japan while on tour in the country, Japanese media said on Friday.

Danko, a bass guitarist and lead singer for the famed group The Band, which broke up in 1976, told Chiba District Court near Tokyo that a package his wife sent to him by courier was supposed to contain medicinal codeine, not heroin, the Daily Yomiuri reported.
"I'm not guilty... It's just a mistake. I did not intend to import drugs," the English-language paper quoted him as telling the court.
Danko, 54, said he had asked his wife by phone to send him some "medication" and thought she would understand that he meant codeine, for which he has a prescription.
"I'm just very surprised that she did something that stupid... But she's from France," Danko was quoted as telling the court through an interpreter.

Japanese police arrested Danko in his hotel room on May 6 on suspicion of drug smuggling after they found 1.25 grams (about a twentieth of an ounce) of heroin hidden in a magazine sent to him by courier from the United States.
Sentencing is scheduled for July 25. If found guilty, Danko could be jailed for up to three years or could be deported.
Danko was on a five-concert tour of Japan which started on April 30 and ended on May 6. The last concert went ahead without him after his arrest.
